title: Prune pass: 6 tooling sidecars (daemon config, compiled snapshots, weight config) archived out of the live graph; did NOT resolve the normalized-Fano finding

claims.statement: Six .lab files loaded as graph nodes were not claims at all -- they were daemon/compiler tooling state that happened to satisfy the loader's 'has an id or falls back to filename' rule. All six were isolated (degree 0) and none carried a receipted confirmed claim.
claims.receipt: daemon_config.json: heartbeat/idle-timeout config with a status field, no claim content. graph_metrics.json: a 2026-08-02 metrics snapshot (node_count 324, mismatch_vector, complexity) -- a measurement ABOUT the graph, not a node IN it. labyrinth_unified.json: a 656169-byte compiled snapshot dated 2026-07-27 embedding 279 nodes verbatim -- a stale full-graph duplicate. metrics.json: scoring weight configuration for the objective function. pdf_mapping.json: an empty stub (kind=note, no content). suggestions.json: compiler-generated edge-pollination suggestions between real evidence-* nodes, itself not a claim.

claims.statement: All six moved to artifacts/.lab/archive/ via git mv, preserving history per Rule 1 (Conservation). The loader's existing glob('*.json') is non-recursive, so the archive subdirectory is excluded from future loads without any code change.
claims.receipt: git mv artifacts/.lab/{daemon_config,graph_metrics,labyrinth_unified,metrics,pdf_mapping,suggestions}.json artifacts/.lab/archive/, verified via git status (all 6 show as renames, not deletions). scripts/build_lab_obsidian_graph.py:161 uses lab_dir.glob('*.json'), confirmed non-recursive against a nested archive/ directory.

claims.statement: Of the 51 isolated (degree-0) nodes measured earlier today, 45 carry a receipted confirmed claim and were left untouched -- they are poorly LINKED, not low-value, and archiving them would have violated the isolated-node guard's own intent (connectivity is a structural property to fix with edges, not a reason to discard evidenced work).
claims.receipt: Filter over all 51 isolated nodes (file-level, promote_claims=False): 45 have at least one claim with status=confirmed and a non-empty receipt/receipts/evidence/proof/verification field; 6 do not. Only the 6 were moved.

claims.statement: This pass did not resolve the normalized-Fano finding from the prior Adapt pass. Fano moved from 15.93 to 15.80 -- noise removal, not the structural reduction the v15 tolerance (trigger at 1.25) calls for.
claims.receipt: Erdos-Renyi null-normalized Fano, matched n/m, 200 draws seed 0: pre-archive 372 nodes/1072 edges -> 15.93; post-archive 367 nodes/1073 edges -> 15.80. Isolated count 51->45 (the 6 archived), dangling 24->28 (edges that previously targeted one of the 6 sidecars are now correctly flagged as pointing at an absent node rather than silently resolving to a non-claim file).
claims.note: Removing degree-0 nodes has almost no effect on a variance-of-degree statistic when the driver is hub fan-out (hub-evidence-oscillations-networks alone carries degree 113 of a 5.76 mean). A Fano-reducing Prune would need to either split or de-fan the hub nodes, or justify the current fan-out as legitimate domain structure and adjust the hub exemption accordingly -- neither was attempted this pass.

issues: The dangling count rose 24->28 as a direct, correct side effect of this prune -- 4 edges previously pointed at now-archived sidecar files and are now honestly flagged rather than silently resolving.
The real Fano-driving structure (three hub-evidence-* nodes at degree 113/80/48) was not touched. A structural Prune targeting hub fan-out is still open.

The loader change that would prevent this class of file (daemon state, compiled snapshots, weight configs) from ever being treated as a node again was NOT made -- only the six known instances were moved. A new sidecar of the same kind would still load as a phantom node.
falsifier: Closed when normalized Fano (excluding declared hub-* nodes) is re-measured below the v15 1.25 trigger, or when the hub exemption is defined precisely enough that the current ~7.8 is defended as legitimate rather than pending reduction.
